notes.title: Occupy Mars: The Game Kickstarter Campaign is now live!
notes.content:
Greetings, Rover Mechanics!

We’re excited to announce that we’re launching a Kickstarter campaign for Occupy Mars: The Game! 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34825804/f2e6958fdb2ab285f371fe20e7c4b220008b719b.png

Occupy Mars: The Game is a highly technical survival game about Mars colonization. As an astronaut who has just landed on the Red Planet, your task is to build and expand your base and survive in the harsh environment that is unlike the one on Earth.

[previewyoutube=ePLA8ljmeaI;full][/previewyoutube]

The game has been in development since 2017 and we’re finally nearing its completion! While Occupy Mars: The Game is almost ready for Early Access release, another challenge lies ahead – pre-release promotion. We have to make sure our voice is heard and the game makes its way to players, which is difficult for our still relatively small team. This campaign’s goal is to reach as many people as possible while gathering additional funds for marketing purposes.

That’s why we need your help!

If you’ve been itching to step out of the hangar and explore the Red Planet in Rover Mechanic Simulator, we can assure you that Occupy mars: The Game will fulfill that wish! Take a look at the campaign page and consider supporting our campaign! Spread the word about the game and share a link on your social media profile – any little thing you can do is a huge help!


 Learn more about the game and the campaign on its dedicated Kickstarter page
 Check out Steam store page of Occupy Mars: The Game

notes.title: Devlog #28: Powering Curiosity
notes.content:
Dear Martians!

We’re continuing our devlog series with another interesting content related to the Curiosity Rover! 

Before you start making repairs, it’s good to learn more about Curiosity's components. The rover equipped with fragile science instruments requires a special power system to provide electricity and heat. That’s why this big robot is equipped with the Multi-Mission Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator (MMRTG), which converts the heat from the natural decay of radioisotope materials to electricity. ⚡

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34825804/789f7ee0bb489be6020c8ee792e855db089629e8.png

MMRTG consist of two elements: a source of heat that contains mostly plutonium-238 dioxide, and thermocouples that convert the plutonium’s decay heat energy to electricity. During your mission, one of your tasks will be to repair this critical device, but it won’t be a problem for you since you’re a great engineer! ⚙️

https://i.imgur.com/h9UQP7Q.gif

Implementing Curiosity Rover to the game will take some time, so please be patient. We will soon provide more information. RMS Team is working hard on this big update that will give you additional hours of the gameplay. Stay tuned! 🤖

Remember about our Community Group Challenge as we’re getting close to reaching the third goal, which will unlock the ability to fix the Mars Helicopter Ingenuity! Feel free to spread a word to more people interested in Mars Rovers and engineering.

notes.title: Devlog #27: Curiosity Jack
notes.content:
Dear Martians!    

We’re back with another awesome devlog for you! 

This time we’d like to talk about fixing Curiosity Rover. As you know from the previous post, our Curiosity consists of 1387 components, including screws and other small elements. But tinkering with those parts will be different than dismantling components from MER Twins or Sojourner Rover. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34825804/f97ad27b500c6188aedb479f857eaf5c36592bc4.png

Since the Curiosity Rover is a car-sized vehicle, you have to use a different type of jack in order to make repairs. Besides, the rover’s internal components have to be dismantled from the bottom, so our design team has to design a jack that allows you to work underneath the vehicle. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34825804/0b84d6ae987d35448bd2de67a2da6291d754b576.png

Our 3d graphic designers modelled the jack based on the reference photos they had priorly collected (mostly from NASA JPL website). Below you can take a look at some of these pictures.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34825804/86b7b51e32c3044e7768f89acba2e29e2846f418.png
(Image: © NASA/JPL-Caltech)

Given the size and weight of new rovers, the original Curiosity jack is a fixed-height structure that lets engineers from JPL and NASA crawl under the vehicle, similar to what you might see in regular car workshops. To make the digital jack fit RMS gameplay-wise, our developers slightly redesigned the jack to make it height-adjustable. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34825804/f4831a6d5dd56d0d1562dd1387d4f9ba21939e81.png

We're working hard on Curiosity Rover Update, which will add the big rover and additional hours of gameplay. Stay tuned and feel free to join our Discord server! Remember also to follow our upcoming game Occupy Mars: The game and add it to your Wishlist. 

https://store.steampowered.com/app/758690/Occupy_Mars_The_Game/

Rover Mechanic Simulator Team

notes.title: Devlog #17: Assembly, Disassembly and Analysis of Mars Exploration Rover Model
notes.content:
https://i.imgur.com/u9E57y4.gif

Dear Martians!

Making repairs of Mars rovers will involve working in three modes: the assembly mode, the disassembly mode and the analysis mode. You will need to employ these modes while using the circuits workbench and optical workbench or while working directly on Mars rovers. In each case, the modes you’ll use will be the same, the only difference will lie in the type of the joining elements you’ll need to remove to disassemble a given part, such as screws, solder alloys, etc. Today’s devlog will focus on the assembly, disassembly and analysis of the Mars Exploration Rover model.

https://i.imgur.com/NDP6ldb.png

Disassembly mode
This mode will be used to remove components from the rover. When you right-click some part of the vehicle, the display will focus on that part and you’ll be able to freely rotate the camera around it. In the bottom right corner of the screen, you’ll see information related to that element (name, image and wear level). If it’s possible to disassemble the part and you hold the right mouse button, it will unlock the screws and cables that will need to be removed in order to detach the component. If it’s not possible to disassemble the part, then the components that block the operation and need to be dismantled will light up in red. The removed element will be stored in the player’s inventory, where it can be destroyed (using the recycling machine), or reattached to a suitable place in the rover.

https://i.imgur.com/n8HHZRw.gif

Assembly mode
In this mode, the parts that can be installed in the rover will be displayed (x-ray images). Camera rotation will work in the same way as in the disassembly mode. After selecting the part that you want to mount, you’ll need to hold the right mouse button. This action will call up a special UI that will let you choose the element you want to attach. Then, the part you selected will appear on the rover and the mode that helps you unfasten the screws and connect the cables will be activated. Once the process is complete, the part will be treated as mounted.

https://i.imgur.com/J6Fjzr1.gif

Analysis mode
In this mode, you’ll be able to check the wear level of each component. A faulty part should be repaired only if its wear level drops below 35%. While analyzing the parts, camera rotation will work in the same way as in the other modes. A right click on a component will display its state of wear.
The red colour will signify the wear level between 0 and 35%.
The yellow colour will indicate the wear level between 36 and 75%.
The green colour will refer to the wear level between 76 and 100%.
Based on an analysis of the state of wear, you’ll decide which parts you want to repair.

https://i.imgur.com/wFjz6pj.gif

notes.title: Devlog #16: The Workbench
notes.content:
https://i.imgur.com/RIMMkRN.gif

Dear Martians! 

The Workbench will allow you to repair broken components of the Printed Circuit Boards (PCB) that are used in Mars rovers. Each rover is equipped with several boards that consist of different elements (coils, resistors, memory etc.). They are susceptible to damage and if they break, the PCB stops working and it needs to be repaired. You can print a new board with all its components or print individual elements that need to be soldered onto the PCB.

https://i.imgur.com/BhmXD9t.gif

Repair process:
Before making repairs, you have to choose the PCB that needs to be fixed. Initially, you don’t get any additional information about the wear levels of specific parts (however, you can guess which parts may be damaged by the appearance of the material). 

The Workbench allows you to work in three modes:

 Disassembly mode: In this mode, you will choose which components you want to disassemble. You must then melt the solder alloy and remove the items from the PCB.

 Assembly mode: In this mode, you can choose which elements you want to mount on the PCB. You must then solder the joints.

 Analysis mode: In this mode, you can check the current state of each component and see if it needs to be repaired. 


https://i.imgur.com/h0dKCXm.gif

While using the workbench, the player first enter the analysis mode to identify the faulty components. Once you’ve checked which elements need to be repaired or replaced, you have to print new parts using the 3D printer. In the disassembly mode, you have to remove the damaged components and then in the assembly mode, you will solder new ones onto the PCB.

notes.title: Devlog #11: 3D Printing and Recycling
notes.content:
https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34825804/344ddaad770c31d86b33ccf90d6491d2ea8585a1.png

Dear Martians! 
 
Making repairs on Mars can be difficult due to limited reserves of spare parts. Since you won’t be able to buy new components or deliver them from Earth, you will have a 3D printer and a recycling machine at your disposal. 
 
https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34825804/e6a0ed41ab23f08b983884c6853095630e7adea5.png

The 3D printer is a device that allows you to print parts of the rover that need to be replaced. The printing process will cost you an amount of raw materials and will be a bit time-consuming. 

https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34825804/faef814bef44107bbc0f9a3e8faefb2a443df194.png

3D printing process:
1. First you open the printer’s menu and select parts that can be printed.
2. You can choose several parts, which will be automatically placed in a queue (max 5 items). The more complicated and valuable the part, the longer the printing process takes. 
3.  While printing, you can for example play a mini-game or do something else to pass the time. The device will be running in the background.
4. The printed parts are placed inside capsules which have to be collected before the items are available in the inventory. When printing is completed, you’ll get a notification. 

https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34825804/4c49cdbea1a0ed32bcdf91b0b90f6c68f04fc3ad.png

Some of the parts removed from rovers are worthless and can’t be repaired. You can destroy them using a recycling machine. The recycling machine  turns the unusable parts into resources that you can later use in 3D printing. The better the condition of the part, the bigger the amount of raw materials that you obtain. 

https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34825804/af4a268e0b3ecc4df57bc35c2bbf994496fbe347.png

The recycling machine immediately destroys the parts when you press the “Destroy” button. The components you select are placed in a queue so that you can look through them before clicking “Destroy”.
 
The recycling process: 
1.  Open a special UI which displays all the parts that are in the inventory. 
2.  Choose which components you want to destroy. Similarly to 3D printing, they are placed in a queue (max 5 items). 
3.  When you press the “Destroy” button, the parts get destroyed and you receive a given amount of raw materials.

https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34825804/91719d2a77a76d49d91f07753ca20077d9663e00.png

notes.title: Devlog #10: DC Motors
notes.content:
https://i.imgur.com/wVsQdvk.png

Dear Martians!

Mars Rovers are equipped with DC motors, which enable them to successfully perform the missions in a harsh conditions of the Red Planet. These components are responsible for the steering mechanism, driving the wheels, rock drilling, operating the robotic arm and controlling the cameras. 

If one of the motors is damaged, rovers can’t work properly and the player’s task will be to repair broken device. This job will require precision and also it will be good to know some basic details of the DC motors! For example, conventional DC motor and the coreless one are used in Mars Rovers, so let’s learn about three main subassemblies of them: the stator, the rotor and the brush system.  

https://i.imgur.com/cDfAr0T.png

Coreless DC motor components:  

 The stator is the main body of the motor that consist of permanent magnet at the centre, the housing, which acts as magnetic return, and the mounting flange.
 The rotor with winding and commutator.
 The brush system with graphite brushes and the electrical motor connections.


Conventional DC motor components: 

 The stator with the permanent magnet, the housing and the mounting flange.
 The rotor with winding and iron core that are mounted on the shaft. On this component there is also the commutator.
 The brush system with the electrical motor connections.


DC motors convert electrical energy into mechanical energy in a form of rotation. The movement is produced by electromagnetism. 

-----

Dear Martians! 

Sojourner is the Mars Pathfinder robotic rover that explored the Martian terrain. It is equipped with large main antenna, APXS and three cameras: two monochrome in front, and a color one in the rear. Delicate components, such as electronics, are housed inside the WEB (Warm Electronic Box).

APXS (Alpha-Particle X-Ray Spectrometer) - instrument used to analyze the rock composition and other surface materials.

Rear camera - color camera that is located on the aft part near the APXS, used to provide spectral information while imaging the APXS target area, rover tracks, and terrain.

WEB (Warm Electronic Box) - "warm box" designed to protect microver’s electronics. 

https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34825804/eb253e80b2d88c07b5992257ca6895054c99fa39.png

notes.title: Devlog #8: The Rover's Antennas
notes.content:
https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34825804/a17ffd76a4a156bb1470e2545eb27f789718464d.png

Dear Martians!

In today's post we would like you to get familiar with Spirit and Opportunity’s antennas that serve as rover’s "voice" and "ears". The rover is equipped with a low-gain and high-gain antenna as well as an UHF antenna that are mounted on the equipment deck.

The low-gain antenna is a long-range antenna that can transmit and receive information in almost every direction. The antenna sends radio waves at a low rate to the Deep Space Network (DSN) antennas on Earth.

https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34825804/e1a6ae4cbc1d80c45e7561ee163e231b7982c1fc.png

The high-gain antenna is a long-range antenna that has a capability to transmit an information in a specific direction.The antenna is steerable and can move to point itself directly to Deep Space Network (DSN) antennas.  

https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34825804/2035ae645a9eb04d51b9cb9c7638c9ad964bb8e6.png

The UHF antenna (ultra-high frequency antenna)  is a close-range antenna that is used to communicate with Earth through NASA's orbiters around Mars. One UHF antenna is mounted on the rover and one is on the petal of the lander. 

https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34825804/fb1249f2082aa6cdb0c905156470568f41e2d918.png

The antennas are a complicated devices that have many tiny elements. These components can be damaged and in that case the antennas won't work properly. Mars rovers without its "ears" and "voice" can't perform their tasks well, so you'll have to repair broken elements.

In today’s post we would like introduce to you essential devices that will help you with the repair process. Let's take a look at overhead crane and hydraulic jack. 

The overhead crane is a device that lifts and moves Mars Rovers. It runs on elevated tracks,  which are basically spread over the entire hangar! The device is equipped with a lifting component - a hoist, which travels along the bridge. It can be moved in two ways: front / back and left / right. 

https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34825804/93ecffe891e5b45d0601757708656a9a5dc7a96a.jpg

Hydraulic jack is a portable device that is used to lift Mars Rovers. The player will be able to freely move the device to the one of several predefined locations, which means that once you put the hydraulic jack in a defined place, you can move it to the different one. 

https://i.imgur.com/Hhw6jbs.gif

First, the player will have to use the overhead crane and place the rover on the hydraulic jack. When the rover is on the lift, the repair mode starts and the player will not be able to control the gantry until the task is finished.

notes.title: Devlog #6: Magnet Array and Calibration Targets
notes.content:
https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34825804/ad5bf83969c02b2373b57d208e960157229568f5.png

Dear Martians! 

In today's post we would like to give you some information about other science instruments mounted on the Spirit and Opportunity rovers - Magnet Array and Calibration Targets. 

Magnet  Array
Magnet Array is an instrument that is used to collect the airborne dust for the analysis by scientific tools that identify the composition of the Red Planet. Magnetic grains in Martian dust are the pieces of the Red Planet's past.

https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34825804/094e50a891a49cdf454c5085bf927ed693370755.png

Each rover is equipped with three sets of magnetic targets: one set of magnets carried by the Rock Abrasion Tool (RAT), a second set of two magnets mounted on the front of the rover, next to the color calibration / sundial, and a third magnet mounted on the top of the rover deck. 
 
https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34825804/90c572a6dacec2472ecdde2de56e86d600f8bd4e.jpg


 Rat magnets -  four magnets carried by the RAT, used to detect magnetic minerals in the rock material;
 Capture magnet - magnet mounted on the front of the rover, designed to capture any magnetic particles.
 Filter magnet - magnet mounted on the front of the rover, designed to capture the most magnetic particles.
 Sweep magnet - mounted on the top of the rover deck, designed to only allows non-magnetic particles to settle in the center of the magnet. 


https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34825804/dda5310d6497345a64ca07e38a671243b2b190d8.jpg

Calibration Targets
The rover is also equipped with Calibration Targets (such as sundial) that are used by instruments to determine accurate colors, brightnesses, and other specific details. 

 Pancam calibration target is in the shape of a sundial, mounted on the rover deck.
 Mössbauer Spectrometer calibration target mounted under the rover solar panels (it can also be used by the APXS). 
 APXS calibration target is on the inside of its dust doors.
 Mini-TES has an internal target located the Pancam Mast Assembly as well as an external target on the deck of the rover near the low-gain antenna.The colored blocks in the corners are used to calibrate the color in images of the Martian landscape. 

https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34825804/4db28caeaeb9a03585a0191044bcc96034c0204a.png

notes.title: Devlog #5: The equipment: Drill-driver and Riveting Tool
notes.content:
https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34825804/cb1087404b94a72cdb5acd0ed9526fc06b419bef.png

Dear Martians!

There are many devices available in the Martian Workshop that will allow you to dismantle and maintain parts of the Mars rovers. At the beginning of the game, all the tools are stored on the shelves. You have to choose the tools that you will use during the repair process and put them in the player’s inventory. Selected tools will be available in the inventory during the quest. 
For example, you will have a drill-driver and riveting tool at your disposal, which work great on jobs requiring precision.

Drill-driver - cordless drill that is mainly used for driving fasteners or screws and removing screws. It is also used for tightening nuts and removing the rivets. The device is equipped with adjustable clutch, that allow you to control the level of torque in order to avoid overdriving a screw or fastener or to prevent damaging delicate parts of the rover. 

https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34825804/4b2662e55a01309b7ab6ac4b5575d1143d3ece27.png

As you progress through the game, you will be able to upgrade a drill-driver, which will make your work more effective. 

https://i.imgur.com/9vyWCNg.gif

Before driving screws or removing screws you have to choose a drill socket: 
- Cross recessed tip socket;
- Flat tip socket;  
- Hex socket;
- Hex shank;

You can adjust the sockets to the drill-driver, which allow you to fasten screws of various size. Each socket is available in three different size (small, medium, large). The game itself sets the right socket, and the player just adjusts the size to the compatible screw. Additionally, you will have the drill bit, which will allow you to remove the rivets from parts of the rover.  

https://i.imgur.com/wThXvK0.gif

Riveting Tool - cordless device, that is only used for setting new rivets. It is equipped with one attachment that will allow to set the rivets. In the later stages of the game, you’ll be able to upgrade the tool, which will make your work more precise. 

https://i.imgur.com/HuF8fj9.gif
-------
The repair process includes three repairing modes: assembly, disassembly, analysis. In each mode the tools will have different functions, but this is the topic for the future devlog! notes.title: Devlog #4: Science Instruments on the Robotic Arm
notes.content:
https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34825804/8175f050ce0a6494d56ae76920420ee4edd527f1.png

Dear Martians!

In previous post, you became familiar with the Spirit and Opportunity’s Pancam Mast Assembly. Today we would like you to learn about science instruments mounted on the Robotic Arm.

Robotic Arm (also called the instrument deployment device, or IDD) is a device mounted on a rover that holds and maneuvers four science instruments: RAT, MI, MB and APXS. At the end of the arm is a cross-shaped turret that holds various tools. It can spin through a 350-degree turning range.

https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34825804/0cad09dd7346505bb1325fcb358f89326047bbd1.png

RAT (Rock Abrasion Tool) - instrument mounted on the robotic arm that is used to remove rock surfaces in order to expose fresh material for the analysis. It grinds away the rock layers. 

MI (Microscopic Imager) - the magnifying glass that takes microscopic images, used to examine the rocks and soils.

https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34825804/beb17fe27e26268721f1e953b3fd6277903852e0.png

MB (Mössbauer Spectrometer) - the instrument used to analyze and characterize the iron in the rocks. It also analyzes magnetic dust samples collected by the Magnetic Array on the rover's deck.

https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34825804/73798721e136fceb0eae567292be5b8f751d3785.png

APXS (Alpha-Particle X-Ray Spectrometer) instrument used to specify the elemental composition of the rocks. It is mounted on the robotic arm and must be placed in contact with the rock surface for the analysis. 

https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34825804/59c5bbc9a4ba28315cbccf70a71ecdcaf0bcf2e9.png

In future devlogs, you will learn about the specific details of other Spirit and Opportunity’s science instruments :)

notes.title: Devlog #3: Pancam Mast Assembly
notes.content:
Dear Martians!

Before you start the repairing process, you have to learn the details of Mars Rovers and their components. Each rover is equipped with various scientific instruments, which are used to acquire specialized information about the conditions on the Red Planet.Today’s post will focus on the Spirit and Opportunity’s Pancam Mast Assembly, which looks like the rover’s “neck and head”.

https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34825804/4cbfe62ad8da2f3250c936e681d97973f8bd2892.png

Pancam (also known as Panoramic Camera) consists two digital cameras used to take 3D panoramic pictures of the Martian landscape. 
The instrument is also used to create a map of the area where the rover lands, which helps with the search for interesting rocks and soil to analyze.

Navcams are black-and-white cameras that used a visible light to take panoramic 3D images. The Navcam is a stereo pair of cameras, each with a 45-degree field of view to support ground navigation planning. 

https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34825804/c61428ee6a13f2faded9fce53cee451a545269d3.png

Mini-TES (Miniature Thermal Emission Spectrometer) - measures the different spectrums of infrared light, or heat, emitted from different minerals in rocks and soils. Mini-TES is also used to look for minerals which formed in the presence of water.

https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34825804/d02535b3e774c44b0fc863c3d222f182a6eadd3a.png

notes.title: Devlog #1: Backstory
notes.content:
Dear Martians! 

When NASA announced that the Opportunity Rover mission officially ended on Feb 13th we were all very sad. This "little rover that could" along with his twin brother Spirit landed on Mars in January 2004. 

Since that time he gave us amazing science and pictures. He was designed to operate for 90 days, but he worked tirelessly for 15 years! 

We thought it's not fair that the Rover is to stay broken on Mars forever and we decided that if there's anything we could do to bring him (and other Mars Rovers) back to life we would do it! 

That's why we are announcing Rover Mechanic Simulator - a new game in the "Occupy Mars" Universe where you play as one of the colonists - an engineer who works in one of the first Mars bases with the goal of fixing all the historic Rovers and Landers that ever landed on the Red Planet.

Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, Curiosity, Phoenix, InSight and more... all of the rovers and landers that ever touched the surface of the Red Planet we want to ultimately add to this game. Learning all the details about their internal components and hundreds of scientific instruments they have on board will be an exciting and fun scientific adventure!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/864680/Rover_Mechanic_Simulator

See also our other game about Mars. Occupy Mars is a completely different game with different mechanics. It's a science-fiction, sandbox, survival game. We know that players who enjoy playing "Mechanic" games usually don't play survival / open-world simulators and we hope that thanks to Rover Mechanic some of you will actually get more interested in Mars exploration as well :) 

Also we want to clarify that by making Rover Mechanic Simulator we are not taking anything away from Occupy Mars - on the contrary - thanks to this second game we were able to grow our team so we can actually do more in both games.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/758690/Occupy_Mars_The_Game
